"""Owner-authorized permanent closure of an unused ordinary spec request key.

Rejection proofs are only a UI trigger, never an authorization capability. Closing
writes recovery metadata, no Run, model budget, business data or artifact.
"""

from pydantic import Field
from sqlalchemy import insert, select

from .contracts import Strict
from .db import (delivery_graph_requests, fingerprint, internal_app_runs,
    internal_instances, internal_releases, internal_run_bindings,
    internal_spec_run_terminals as journal, runs)
from .errors import DomainError


class OriginalRequest(Strict):
    # Revision zero is the finite VALIDATION_NOT_STARTED subset. No coercion.
    expected_revision: int = Field(ge=0, strict=True)
    expected_release_fingerprint: str = Field(pattern=r"^[a-f0-9]{64}$")
    input: dict
    request_key: str = Field(min_length=1, max_length=100)
    expected_owner_goal_binding_fingerprint: str | None = Field(default=None, pattern=r"^[a-f0-9]{64}$")


class CloseInput(Strict):
    release_id: str = Field(pattern=r"^irelease_[a-f0-9]{32}$")
    request: OriginalRequest


def fenced(c, user, iid, key):
    return c.execute(select(journal.c.request_key).where(journal.c.instance_id == iid,
        journal.c.principal_id == user, journal.c.request_key == key)).first() is not None


def _scope(store, c, user, iid):
    row = c.execute(select(internal_instances.c.project_id,
        internal_instances.c.source_app_id).where(internal_instances.c.id == iid,
        internal_instances.c.principal_id == user)).mappings().first()
    if row is None:
        raise DomainError("PERMISSION_DENIED")
    store.lock_project(c, user, row["project_id"])
    return row


def _absent(c, user, iid, key):
    # Scalar identities only. A partial accepted pair is never absence. A stray
    # binding has lost its key, so conservatively block closure for this instance.
    if c.execute(select(internal_app_runs.c.id).where(internal_app_runs.c.instance_id == iid,
            internal_app_runs.c.request_key == key)).first():
        raise DomainError("OUTCOME_UNKNOWN", "Accepted AppRun evidence exists; read original key")
    if c.execute(select(delivery_graph_requests.c.request_key).where(
            delivery_graph_requests.c.app_id == iid,
            delivery_graph_requests.c.request_key == key)).first():
        raise DomainError("OUTCOME_UNKNOWN", "Request ledger evidence exists")
    bindings = c.execute(select(internal_run_bindings.c.run_id,
        internal_run_bindings.c.app_run_id).where(
        internal_run_bindings.c.snapshot["instance_id"].as_string() == iid).limit(129)).all()
    if len(bindings) > 128:
        raise DomainError("OUTCOME_UNKNOWN", "Recovery metadata scan budget exhausted")
    for rid, aid in bindings:
        app = c.execute(select(internal_app_runs.c.instance_id, internal_app_runs.c.principal_id,
            internal_app_runs.c.request_key).where(internal_app_runs.c.id == aid)).first()
        header = c.execute(select(runs.c.principal_id, runs.c.request_key).where(runs.c.id == rid)).first()
        if (app is None or header is None or app.instance_id != iid or app.principal_id != user
                or header.principal_id != user or header.request_key != "internal:" + aid
                or app.request_key == key):
            raise DomainError("OUTCOME_UNKNOWN", "Accepted identities incomplete or conflicting")


def _receipt(row):
    value = {k: row[k] for k in ("instance_id", "principal_id", "request_key", "project_id",
        "app_id", "release_id", "request")}
    try:
        request = OriginalRequest.model_validate(value["request"]).model_dump(exclude_unset=True)
    except ValueError as exc:
        raise DomainError("VERSION_CONFLICT") from exc
    if (request != value["request"] or request["input"] != {}
            or request["request_key"] != value["request_key"]
            or fingerprint(value) != row["fingerprint"]):
        raise DomainError("VERSION_CONFLICT")
    return dict(namespace="spec-run-terminal.v1", status="CLOSED_NOT_ACCEPTED", **value,
        wire_request_fingerprint=fingerprint(request), new_model_requests=0, project_writes=0)


def read(store, c, user, iid, key):
    scope = _scope(store, c, user, iid)
    row = c.execute(select(journal).where(journal.c.instance_id == iid,
        journal.c.principal_id == user, journal.c.request_key == key)).mappings().first()
    if row is None:
        return None
    if row["project_id"] != scope["project_id"] or row["app_id"] != scope["source_app_id"]:
        raise DomainError("VERSION_CONFLICT")
    _absent(c, user, iid, key)
    return _receipt(row)


def close(store, user, iid, key, body):
    request = body.request.model_dump(exclude_unset=True)
    if request["request_key"] != key or request["input"] != {} or (
            "expected_owner_goal_binding_fingerprint" in request and
            request["expected_owner_goal_binding_fingerprint"] is None):
        raise DomainError("INVALID_INPUT", "Only frozen empty-input ordinary spec metadata is supported")
    with store.tx() as c:
        scope = _scope(store, c, user, iid)
        prior = read(store, c, user, iid, key)
        if prior:
            if prior["release_id"] != body.release_id or prior["request"] != request:
                raise DomainError("VERSION_CONFLICT")
            return prior
        # No material or accepted body reads; original release family and scope only.
        from .pa_spec_apps import FAMILIES
        release = c.execute(select(internal_releases.c.snapshot["draft"]["id"].as_string().label("app"),
            internal_releases.c.snapshot["draft"]["candidate"]["namespace"].as_string().label("family"))
            .where(internal_releases.c.id == body.release_id,
                internal_releases.c.project_id == scope["project_id"],
                internal_releases.c.principal_id == user)).mappings().first()
        if release is None or release["app"] != scope["source_app_id"] or release["family"] not in FAMILIES:
            raise DomainError("PERMISSION_DENIED")
        _absent(c, user, iid, key)
        row = dict(instance_id=iid, principal_id=user, request_key=key,
            project_id=scope["project_id"], app_id=scope["source_app_id"],
            release_id=body.release_id, request=request)
        row["fingerprint"] = fingerprint(row)
        c.execute(insert(journal).values(**row))
        return _receipt(row)

"""SQLite authenticated API/actual Worker proof, no real model or private diagnostics."""

from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
from threading import Event

import pytest
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from sqlalchemy import event, func, select

from sim2act.api import create_app
from sim2act.db import (Store, fingerprint, internal_app_runs, internal_run_bindings,
    internal_spec_run_terminals, runs)
from sim2act.worker import Worker
from test_pa_spec_apps import setup, generate, confirm, instance


def test_original_key_permanent_terminal(env, monkeypatch):
    data = setup(env)
    store, settings, client, user, pid, *_ = data
    rid, result, sent = generate(data)
    made = confirm(data, rid, result)
    assert made.status_code == 200, made.text
    release, inst = instance(data, made.json()["id"])
    prefix = f"/api/internal/instances/{inst['id']}"

    def request(key, revision=None):
        return dict(expected_revision=inst["revision"] if revision is None else revision,
            expected_release_fingerprint=release["fingerprint"], input={}, request_key=key)

    def close(body, actor=client):
        return actor.post(prefix + f"/spec-run-requests/{body['request_key']}/close",
            json=dict(release_id=release["id"], request=body))

    def read(key, actor=client):
        return actor.get(prefix + f"/spec-run-requests/{key}")

    def counts():
        with store.engine.connect() as c:
            return [c.execute(select(func.count()).select_from(t)).scalar_one()
                for t in (runs, internal_app_runs, internal_run_bindings)]

    baseline = counts()
    for key, revision, phase in [("rolled-back", 999, "TX_ROLLED_BACK"),
            ("validation", 0, "VALIDATION_NOT_STARTED")]:
        body = request(key, revision)
        rejected = client.post(prefix + "/runs", json=body)
        proof = rejected.json().get("submission_rejection") or rejected.json()["error"]["submission_rejection"]
        assert proof["phase"] == phase and proof["request_fingerprint"] == fingerprint(body)
        assert read(key).json()["error"]["code"] == "OUTCOME_UNKNOWN"
        response = close(body)
        assert response.status_code == 200, response.text
        receipt = read(key).json()
        assert receipt == response.json() and receipt["status"] == "CLOSED_NOT_ACCEPTED"
        assert receipt["request"] == body and receipt["wire_request_fingerprint"] == fingerprint(body)
        assert receipt["app_id"] == made.json()["id"] and receipt["principal_id"] == user
        assert close(body).json() == receipt
        assert client.post(prefix + "/runs", json=request(key)).status_code == 409
        assert close(request(key, 2)).status_code == 409
    assert counts() == baseline
    assert len(sent) == 3  # Only fixture generation uses the explicit mock transport.

    with TestClient(create_app(store, settings)) as foreign:
        foreign.headers["Authorization"] = "Bearer synthetic-test-B"
        assert close(request("wrong-owner"), foreign).status_code == 403
        assert read("rolled-back", foreign).status_code == 403
    invalid = request("unsupported"); invalid["input"] = {"x": "not empty"}
    assert close(invalid).status_code == 400
    malformed = request("bad-wire"); malformed["expected_revision"] = "invalid"
    assert close(malformed).status_code == 422
    assert read("bad-wire").json()["error"]["code"] == "OUTCOME_UNKNOWN"

    # Failure after insert must roll back the terminal; no partial success.
    def fail_insert(conn, cursor, statement, parameters, context, executemany):
        if statement.startswith("INSERT INTO internal_spec_run_terminals"):
            raise RuntimeError("synthetic terminal insert failure")
    event.listen(store.engine, "after_cursor_execute", fail_insert)
    try:
        with pytest.raises(RuntimeError, match="synthetic terminal insert failure"):
            close(request("failed-close"))
    finally:
        event.remove(store.engine, "after_cursor_execute", fail_insert)
    assert read("failed-close").json()["error"]["code"] == "OUTCOME_UNKNOWN" and counts() == baseline

    # Actual two-thread transactions, forced lock order in each direction. Each
    # second transaction enters while the winner still owns its project lock.
    for winner in ("close", "enqueue"):
        body = request("race-" + winner)
        entered, release_lock, second_started = Event(), Event(), Event()
        original_lock = store.lock_project
        first = [True]

        def gate(c, principal, project):
            value = original_lock(c, principal, project)
            if first[0]:
                first[0] = False; entered.set()
                assert release_lock.wait(10)
            return value

        def action(kind):
            if kind == "close":
                return close(body)
            return client.post(prefix + "/runs", json=body)

        monkeypatch.setattr(store, "lock_project", gate)
        try:
            with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=2) as pool:
                a = pool.submit(action, winner)
                assert entered.wait(10)
                def second():
                    second_started.set()
                    return action("enqueue" if winner == "close" else "close")
                b = pool.submit(second)
                assert second_started.wait(10)
                release_lock.set()
                result_a, result_b = a.result(timeout=20), b.result(timeout=20)
        finally:
            release_lock.set()
            monkeypatch.setattr(store, "lock_project", original_lock)
        assert result_a.status_code == (200 if winner == "close" else 202), result_a.text
        assert result_b.status_code == (409 if winner == "close" else 400), result_b.text
        receipt = read(body["request_key"])
        assert receipt.status_code == 200, receipt.text
        if winner == "enqueue":
            assert receipt.json()["namespace"] == "spec-run-request.v1"
            assert Worker(store, settings).once()
            assert read(body["request_key"]).json()["status"] == "SUCCEEDED"
        else:
            assert receipt.json()["namespace"] == "spec-run-terminal.v1"

    # A new Store/app over the same committed SQLite DB recovers metadata without
    # initialization, old revision execution, or model calls.
    restarted = Store(str(store.engine.url), test_only=True)
    try:
        with TestClient(create_app(restarted, settings)) as fresh:
            fresh.headers["Authorization"] = "Bearer synthetic-test-A"
            assert read("rolled-back", fresh).json()["status"] == "CLOSED_NOT_ACCEPTED"
            assert fresh.post(prefix + "/runs", json=request("rolled-back")).status_code == 409
    finally:
        restarted.engine.dispose()
    with store.engine.connect() as c:
        assert c.execute(select(func.count()).select_from(internal_spec_run_terminals)).scalar_one() == 3

# Ordinary spec original-key terminal — implementation pending final verification

Baseline: `8268486f5f2c3df6968d7dd38f3bb50f797c53df`.
Local branch: `dev/ordinary-spec-rejection-terminal-20261016`.
Root is the sole product writer; cold_proof_review is read-only.
Implementation is uncommitted and unpushed. This is not a release/acceptance report.

## Contract

Previously A forgot the durable intent after a transient NOT_ACCEPTED rejection.
B correctly retained its cached original key after storage deletion, but could
only read OUTCOME_UNKNOWN forever. Storage deletion is not acceptance evidence.

`spec_run_terminals.py` adds authenticated owner-authorized close of an unused
ordinary spec key. Client rejection proofs are a UI trigger, not a server-side
authorization capability. Close independently checks ownership, original release
family/scope and absence of accepted identities inside the existing project lock
and transaction. Enqueue checks the permanent `(principal, instance, key)` fence
under that same project lock before dispatch; changed DTOs cannot revive it.
Accepted evidence wins: close refuses and the existing accepted GET is unchanged.
Conflicting/partial accepted identities and exhausted metadata scan budget stay
UNKNOWN. The scan is conservatively bounded at 128 instance bindings.

An explicit Store.initialize migration creates `internal_spec_run_terminals`.
API/Worker startup does not initialize/migrate automatically. Close writes only
immutable recovery metadata, with an integrity fingerprint. It does not create
a Run, consume model budget, write business project data or emit an artifact.
Terminal GET freshly authorizes owner/project metadata and verifies scope and
integrity without requiring old materials/current execution qualification. The
existing accepted-receipt authorization remains intact.

Finite wire DTO: exact empty input, request key, integer revision >= 0, release
fingerprint and optional non-null owner-goal fingerprint, plus original release
ID in the close envelope. Revision zero covers a finite backend validation-error
case. Arbitrary malformed DTOs are unsupported and retain UNKNOWN. Browser durable
records still require revision >= 1; the browser validation-phase test is a
synthetic proof protocol test, not proof that the actual UI emits revision zero.
The raw wire DTO fingerprint is distinct from the accepted execution fingerprint.

The UI now requests close only after its existing strict transient proof check,
then authenticates original-key GET. It verifies terminal namespace/status/full
scope/original release/key/exact DTO/wire hash and zero execution claims. Clearing
still occurs under the nonqueued Web Lock, current identity/workspace/instance
generation checks and exact local-record comparison. Lost/failed close preserves
UNKNOWN; subsequent actions only GET the original key. No storage event unlocks it.

## Actual evidence and remaining work

Evidence root: `/workspace/ordinary-rejection-evidence-20261016`.

- Baseline RED: `red-protocol.json`/stdout/stderr, strict TX_ROLLED_BACK proof
  did not request closure. Actual page scripts, synthetic HTTP/shared adapter.
- First implementation protocol attempt failed because of the API helper call
  signature; preserved as `green-protocol-1.*`, fixed in source.
- `green-protocol-2.json`: PASS, 10 checks, 4 execution POSTs, 4 close attempts,
  8 GETs. Covers both proof phases, A/B cached-key recovery without storage
  events, close failure, forged deletion and wrong receipt principal. Its final
  late-GET assertion was inadequate and is superseded, not accepted as evidence.
- Backend attempts 1/2 failed test expectations: actual confirm is HTTP 200 rather
  than 201, and OUTCOME_UNKNOWN is HTTP 400 rather than 409. Logs/XML and lossless
  per-case SQLite archives retained in backend-1/2 and cases-1/2.
- Backend attempt 3 command targeted the single test in
  `tests/test_spec_run_terminals.py`; the process completed with exit code 0
  (write_stdin session 54480). Logs/XML are backend-3.* and case archive cases-3.
  Their full contents have not been reread after completion because of ENOSPC.
  The test covers authenticated API proof phases, permanent changed-DTO fence,
  actual authenticated fixture-B denial, unsupported malformed wire metadata,
  INSERT-after-execution rollback injection, actual concurrent SQLite transactions
  in both forced lock orders, actual deterministic Worker success for the accepted
  winner, and a new Store/app recovering the committed SQLite database.
- Independent static protocol review:
  `/workspace/ordinary-rejection-review-20261016/PROTOCOL_REVIEW.md`.
  Review identified the pre-insert injection and weak late-GET assertion; injection
  was corrected before backend attempt 3. The late-GET test was corrected afterward
  to replace a record at the exact original scope key while GET waits, switch
  identity, and compare both replacement bytes and UI. That revision is NOT RUN.

Concrete blocker: new exec_command startup fails before running the requested
command, `failed to register synthetic bubblewrap mount target /tmp/.codex:
No space left on device (os error 28)`. No authorization rejection, permission
expansion, environment substitution or removal of older sealed evidence occurred.
The previous complete evidence archive in /tmp remains preserved.

corrected protocol and existing recovery regressions, complete independent review,
check diff/protected files, commit and normal-push this development branch, then
verify remote exact SHA and clean local/upstream difference. No push was attempted.
Native browser, Windows, PostgreSQL, source-version upgrade, full P-A/P-B, real

force push, new credentials or security permission changes.
